texts.facts: Vide this judgmentcumaward, I proceed to decide the DAR which is treated as claim petition u/s 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, as amended uptodate (hereinafter referred to as the Act) for grant of compensation in a road accident. 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 25.09.2013 at about 10.00 hrs. while the petitioner was coming back to Mehram Nagar and was crossing the road near Mehram Nagar, Police Colony, suddenly an Accent car bearing No.DL1RX7100 came from T3 side in a very high speed and Manchan Mandal vs Suresh Singh on 20 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155092720/ 1 being driven very rashly and negligently and hit the taxi of the petitioner on the left side, thereby inflicting grievous injuries on the body of the petitioner and also damaging his taxi. It is averred that the petitioner was taken to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi by the PCR van where he was hospitalized and treated. It is averred that due to the said accident the petitioner had sustained fourteen stitches on his head apart from other injuries and was got discharged the next day. It is averred that the said accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the respondent No.1 of the offending vehicle who was driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner without safety of the others and in violation of the traffic rules and norms. It is averred that the respondents are severally as well as jointly liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. It is stated that in respect of the accident FIR No.320/13 under Sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt. It is averred that the petitioner and his family Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 2 of 27 members have suffered from mental pain, agony and also from economic losses. It is averred that at the time of the accident the petitioner was working as a taxi driver and he was earning Rs.14,000/ per month. It is averred that during the period of his medical treatment Rs.10,000/ was spent on medicine and the petitioner had spent Rs.15,000/ on conveyance and Rs.15,000/ on special diet. 3. Written statement was filed on behalf of the respondent No.2 taking the preliminary objections that the compensation as claimed by the petitioner is excessive, exorbitant and based on imaginary and sentimental grounds and the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the claim, as claimed. It is averred that the vehicle bearing registration No.DL1RX7100 Accent Car was insured with Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd. having its office at 9th Floor Videocon Tower Jhandewalan Extension, Delhi vide Commercial vehicle Insurance Cover Note No.52150449 and certificate No.3368/00467417/000/01 valid from 05.10.2012 to 04.10.2013 and under the vicarious liability the insurance company is liable to pay the claim to the petitioner, if any. It is averred that the vehicle bearing registration No.DL1RX7100 was handed over by the respondent No.2 to one Shri Suresh Singh S/o Shri Rajan Singh R/o D117, Sector7, Dwarka Papan Kalan, New Delhi under an agreement after taking driving test of Shri Suresh Kumar who had also submitted his DL and the respondent No.2 believing the DL submitted by Shri Suresh Singh to be valid, had handed over the vehicle to him. It is averred that the respondent No. Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 3 of 27 2 has no liability whatsoever, as against the petitioner and the liability, if any, is either of the insurance company or of Shri Suresh Singh. It is stated that although the respondent No.2 is the registered owner of Hyundai Car bearing registration No.DL1RX7100 Hyundai Accent Car, but the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner. It is averred that there is no breach of the terms of the policy or violation of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2. 4. Written submissions were filed on behalf of the insurance company denying negligence on the part of the insured vehicle. It is stated that the vehicle bearing No.DL7RX7100 was insured with the company vide policy No.3368/00467417/000/01. It is averred that the company has noticed breach in the terms of the policy. It is averred that the petitioner was admitted in Safdarjung Hospital and as per the MLC the petitioner had suffered simple injuries. It is averred that the IO had impounded the driving license of the driver which was alleged to have been issued from Delhi and had filed the report as per which no record was found for the said DL. This issue is accordingly decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents. Issue No.2 17. The petitioner in paras 2, 5 and 6 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A had deposed to that effect. On behalf of the respondent No.2 Shri Kartik, Executive Liasoning entered into the witness box as R2W1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.R2W1/A reiterating the averments made in the written statement filed on behalf of the respondent No.2. He stated that there was no breach of Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 5 of 27 the terms of the policy or violation of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the respondent No.2. He stated that the DL, RC, Fitness Certificate, Permit and Insurance Policy had been seized by the police and the same are Mark R2W1/1 (colly). On behalf of the respondent No.3, Shri Jitender Dhabhai, Legal Officer entered into the witness box as R3W1 and he relied on copy of notice under Order 12 rule 8 CPC which is Ex.R3W1/1, copy of receipt of notice which is Ex.R3W1/2, attested copy of policy along with terms and conditions which is Ex.R3W1/3 and copy of report of DL which is Ex.R3W1/4. He stated that as per the report filed by the IO in the DAR, he found no records in the RTO Mayur Vihar, Phase1, Delhi regarding the DL of the driver. As the case is U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver." Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh It is established law that in a claim petition under Motor Vehicle Act, the standard of proof to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle is not at par with the criminal case where such rashness and negligence is required to be proved beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt. In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the Manchan Mandal vs Suresh Singh on 20 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155092720/ 4 part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. 12. The case of the petitioner is that on 25.09.2013 at about 10.00 hrs. while the petitioner was coming back to Mehram Nagar and was crossing the road near Mehram Nagar, Police Colony, suddenly an Accent car bearing No.DL1RX7100 came from T3 side in a very high speed and being driven very rashly and negligently and hit the taxi of the petitioner on the left side, thereby inflicting grievous injuries on the body of the petitioner and also damaging his taxi. It was averred that the petitioner was taken to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi by the PCR van where he was hospitalized and treated. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing the accident. Thus it stands established that Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 12 of 27 the petitioner had sustained injuries in the alleged accident. In addition, he is further entitled to non pecuniary damages/general damages which include (1) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries and (2) loss of expectation of life. It was averred that the petitioner and his family members had suffered from mental pain, agony and also from economic losses. It was averred that during the period of his medical treatment Rs.10,000/ was spent on medicine and the petitioner had spent Rs. 15,000/ on conveyance and Rs.15,000/ on special diet. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the nature of injuries was opined to be simple. However there is nothing to show that the petitioner had sustained any disability in the accident. Thus the petitioner had not got any disability due to the accident. It cannot be disputed that the petitioner had sustained injuries and underwent treatment for the same. The petitioner had stated that he had spent an amount of Rs.10,000/ on medicine. The petitioner had filed bills for an amount of Rs. 1,383/ approximately. Looking to the nature of the injuries the petitioner is held entitled to the amount of the bills. The petitioner would incur some expenses even subsequently. Accordingly an amount of Rs.2,000/ is awarded towards medical treatment and expenses including the amount of the bills. 19A. Note can also be taken of the fact that on account of the accident the petitioner may not have been able to perform his day to day duties towards his family and may not have been able to enjoy the amenities of life and would have undergone pain and suffering. No document has been placed on record regarding expenditure on conveyance, special diet or attendant charges. During crossexamination by the learned counsel for the insurance company Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 15 of 27 PW1 denied the suggestion that he had spent Rs.15,000/ on conveyance or Rs.15,000/ on special diet. There is also nothing to show any expenditure on these counts. There is also nothing to show that the injuries of the petitioner were such that he might have to incur extra expenditure on special diet or attendant charges. He stated that currently he was in the same Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 16 of 27 profession. He admitted that due to the accident he had not suffered any future loss towards his earning. The petitioner has not proved that he acquired any disability on account of the accident or that he is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce his efficiency to work and thereby he would suffer loss of future income. In fact during crossexamination PW1 stated that currently he was in the same profession. Even during examination by the Tribunal the petitioner stated that even at present he was driving the vehicle and was earning the same amount (as at the time of the accident). Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future income. The issue was considered at length by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Sanjay v. Suresh Chand & Ors. and it was observed: "The issue of satisfying the third party liability even in case of breach of the terms of insurance policy is settled by three Judge Bench report in Sohan Lal Passi v. P. Sesh Reddy, (1996) 5 SCC 21. As per Section 149(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act (the Act), an insurer is entitled to defend the action on the grounds as mentioned under Section 149(2)(a) Manchan Mandal vs Suresh Singh on 20 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155092720/ 10 (i)(ii) of the Act. Thus, the onus is on the insurer to prove that there is breach of the condition of the policy. Even if a conscious breach on the part of the insured is established, still the insurer has a statutory liability to pay the compensation to the third party and will simply have the right to recover the same from the insured/tortfeasor either in the same proceedings or by independent proceedings as the case may be, as ordered by the Claims Tribunal or the Court." Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 21 of 27 Thus if the insurance company proves conscious breach of the terms of the policy, then only it would be entitled to recovery rights. In the instant case it was argued on behalf of the respondent No.2 that the respondent No.2 had taken all reasonable care before engaging respondent No.1 as a driver. In the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in MAC APP 2/2005 New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Mithlesh & Ors. decided on 1.5.2012 reference was made to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Swaran Singh (2004) 3 SCC 297 where it was held as under: "SUMMARY OF FINDINGS: 106. (v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how said burden would be discharged, inasmuch as the same would depend upon Suit No. D79/14 Manchan Mandal v Suresh Singh Page no. 24 of 27 the facts and circumstance of each case. (vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy, condition regarding holding of a valid license by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards insured unless the Manchan Mandal vs Suresh Singh on 20 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155092720/ 12 said breach or breaches on the condition of driving license is/ are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident. (vii) The question as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving license produced by the driver, (a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfil the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case." The Hon'ble Supreme Court in PEPSU Road Transport Corporation v. National Insurance Company 2013 (4) TAC 16 (SC) held as under: "8. In a claim for compensation, it is certainly open to the insurer under Section 149(2)(a)(ii) to take a defence that the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident was not duly licensed.
